Select internal connections in a linked emulator

Source: R/prunlgp.R
prunlgp.Rd

Select input subsets for scalar component emulators using validation predictions from the complete linked network. The initial network remains eligible throughout the search.

Usage

prunlgp(
  object,
  emulators,
  x,
  y,
  refit,
  weights = NULL,
  scale = NULL,
  objective = NULL,
  protect = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  search = c("subsets", "backward"),
  visit_order = NULL,
  max_evals = 200L,
  max_rounds = NULL,
  min_improvement = 0,
  tolerance = 1e-10,
  seed = 1L,
  B = object$specs$B,
  M = 50L,
  workers = 1L,
  threads = 1L,
  worker_init = NULL,
  verb = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'prunlgp'
predict(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'prunlgp'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'prunlgp'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

An lgp object defining the initial network.

emulators

The original list of fitted scalar gp or dgp components. Component IDs must match object. Their data$X columns use the original To_Input numbering. Multi-output components must first be split into scalar emulators.

x

Numeric matrix of validation global inputs, in the original global column numbering. No observed internal outputs are supplied for prediction.

y

Named list of validation response vectors, keyed by emulator ID. Only these outputs contribute to scoring and protection.

refit

Function function(model, keep, seed) returning a newly fitted emulator with the same ID and response as model, trained on model$data$X[, keep, drop = FALSE]. keep refers to original columns. Set the fitting budget, kernel and other parameters explicitly in this function. It must not use validation responses or modify its input model.

weights

Nonnegative scoring weights, named like y. Defaults to equal weights. At least one weight must be positive.

scale

Positive output scales, named like y. Defaults to the sample standard deviations of component training responses. Supply a meaningful positive scale explicitly for constant training responses.

objective

Optional function function(rmse, scale, weights) returning one finite numeric loss to minimise. Defaults to weighted mean NRMSE.

protect

Optional nonnegative relative RMSE tolerance, either scalar or named like y. Each scored output must remain within this tolerance of its initial validation RMSE. A zero initial error permits only numerical tolerance. NULL applies no per-output protection.

groups

Optional named character vector mapping emulator IDs to shared fitting groups. Copies in a group must have identical training data and original input dimensions. Deleting an input removes that dimension from every copy, including an origin copy supplied through Global.

search

Either "subsets", visiting each group and evaluating all original internal-input subsets, or "backward", evaluating single-input deletions from the current network. Both use the system validation loss.

visit_order

Group IDs in the desired visiting order for "subsets". Defaults to first occurrence in topological order.

max_evals

Maximum network evaluations, including the initial and all-internal-inputs-removed networks. Defaults to 200.

max_rounds

Maximum full passes (subsets) or accepted deletions (backward). Defaults to one pass for subsets and unlimited for backward.

min_improvement

Minimum absolute loss reduction for a non-tied search transition. Defaults to zero. The final choice compares all evaluated admissible networks, including smaller improvements.

tolerance

Absolute numerical tolerance for score ties and protection. Ties prefer fewer internal connections, then the lexicographic retained-input key.

seed

Positive integer controlling fitting, linking and prediction.

B

Number of linked imputations; defaults to object$specs$B.

M

Prediction conditioning-set size; defaults to 50.

workers

Number of PSOCK processes for independent candidates. Functions supplied by the caller must be serialisable and self-contained.

threads

Python numerical threads per process. Defaults to one.

worker_init

Optional zero-argument function initialising Python in each worker, for example function() init_py(dgpsi_ver = "dev"). The default calls init_py() with its default environment.

verb

Print accepted moves and completion information.

...

Arguments forwarded to the selected model's method.

Value

A list of class prunlgp, containing model (an ordinary lgp), initial_model (the initial network activated with the same settings), emulators, initial_structure, structure, kept_inputs, initial_score, score, initial_rmse, rmse, validation, history, settings and stop_reason. predict() and summary() delegate to the selected linked model. The history includes failed and rejected candidates.

Details

Every candidate is fitted from the original component training data. Other fitted parameters stay fixed, and predictions are recomputed through the entire network using native linked uncertainty propagation. Component copies can be tied through groups; candidate inputs are then the union of dimensions receiving internal predictions in any copy.

An additional empty-internal-input candidate is evaluated without changing the starting point of the search. A component must retain at least one input; a candidate removing its last input is recorded as failed. Global inputs outside grouped internal dimensions are always retained.

The returned network has the lowest admissible loss among evaluated networks, with ties resolved as above. This is a validation search, not a guarantee of a global optimum or lower test error. Use a separate test set. Fitting seeds are fixed within each group. Linked imputations use a separate stream for each component ID, so removing an unrelated connection does not change that component's imputations. Predictions still propagate native means and variances through every retained connection. R's random state is restored on exit. The Python random state and thread setting are set explicitly and are not restored.

Unlike prune(), which operates inside a DGP, this function removes dependencies between scalar component emulators.

Author

Chaoqun Zhuang

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# See vignette("prunlgp") for a complete executable example.
result <- prunlgp(network, components, x_validation, y_validation,
  refit = function(model, keep, seed) {
    set_seed(seed)
    gp(model$data$X[, keep, drop = FALSE], model$data$Y,
       name = "sexp", id = model$id, verb = FALSE)
  })
predict(result, x_test, full_layer = TRUE)
summary(result)
result$history
} # }
